cards.title: The base form after necessity
cards.body: English has almost lost its subjunctive, but one frame keeps it alive and C1 writing runs on that frame. After an adjective of necessity — essential, vital, important, imperative, crucial, necessary, advisable, desirable — the that-clause takes the bare base form of the verb. It is essential that he arrive on time. Not arrives. The third-person -s does not appear, and be stays be for every person. Czech says the same thing with aby, which is a clean signal to look for: where a Czech sentence would take aby, an English one takes the base form here.
cards.body_cz: Angličtina svůj konjunktiv téměř ztratila, ale jedna vazba jej drží při životě a psaní na úrovni C1 na ní stojí. Po přídavném jméně nutnosti — essential, vital, important, imperative, crucial, necessary, advisable, desirable — má vedlejší věta s that holý základní tvar slovesa. It is essential that he arrive on time. Nikoli arrives. Koncovka třetí osoby se neobjeví a be zůstává be pro všechny osoby. Čeština totéž vyjádří spojkou aby, což je spolehlivý signál: tam, kde by česká věta měla aby, má zde anglická základní tvar.

table.caption: the trigger and what follows it
rows: that each student sign the form.
that he not miss the train.

points: A past trigger changes nothing: it was essential that he arrive keeps the base form.
Be is the form for every person and number, singular or plural.
British English also allows should: it is essential that he should arrive. American English does not.

cards.title: Necessity, not fact
cards.body: The subjunctive belongs to necessity. An adjective that reports a fact takes the ordinary indicative instead, and putting the base form there is as wrong as leaving it out of the frame above. It is clear that he knows the rules — knows, with its -s, because nothing is being demanded. The test is simple: ask whether the that-clause describes something that is so, or something that somebody wants to be so.
cards.body_cz: Konjunktiv patří k nutnosti. Přídavné jméno, které sděluje fakt, si žádá běžný oznamovací způsob a základní tvar je zde stejnou chybou, jakou je jeho vynechání ve vazbě výše. It is clear that he knows the rules — knows s koncovkou, protože se nic nežádá. Test je jednoduchý: zeptejte se, zda vedlejší věta popisuje něco, co je, nebo něco, co si někdo přeje, aby bylo.

table.caption: two families of adjective
rows: It is essential that he arrive.
It is clear that he arrives late.
It is important that she know.
It is obvious that she needs time.
It is vital that the letter be sent.
It is true that the letter was sent.

points: Necessity adjectives: essential · vital · important · imperative · crucial · necessary · advisable · desirable.
Fact adjectives: clear · obvious · true · certain · well known.
Important sits in both families — it is important that he arrive demands, it is important that he arrives first states.

cards.title: After the noun as well
cards.body: The nouns built from these verbs and adjectives carry the pattern with them: a recommendation, a requirement, a demand, a proposal, an insistence, a request, a condition. His demand that the money be returned — not is returned, and not was returned, even though the demand itself is over. This is the shape of contracts, minutes and official letters, and it is the one where a wrong tense slips through unnoticed, because the sentence still reads.
cards.body_cz: Podstatná jména odvozená od těchto sloves a přídavných jmen si vazbu nesou s sebou: a recommendation, a requirement, a demand, a proposal, an insistence, a request, a condition. His demand that the money be returned — nikoli is returned, ani was returned, přestože sám požadavek už je minulostí. Takto vypadají smlouvy, zápisy a úřední dopisy a právě zde špatný čas projde nepovšimnut, protože věta i tak dává smysl.

table.caption: noun + that + base form
rows: that the office move to Brno.
that the shop close on Sunday.
that the work be finished by June.

points: The that-clause after these nouns is appositive: no comma, and that cannot become which.
Our recommendation is that the price not be increased — the negative stays bare here too.
The noun frame is more formal than the verb frame and is the natural one in writing.

cards.title: The form: three rules and no auxiliaries
cards.title_cz: Tvar: tři pravidla a žádná pomocná slovesa
cards.body: Everything about the form is covered by three rules, and each of them looks like a mistake anywhere else in English. First, the verb is the bare base — no -s in the third person. Second, be is the form for every person, and the passive is be plus the past participle, where an ordinary clause would need is or was. Third, the negative is a bare not in front of the verb with no auxiliary at all: that he not be told. Does not and doesn't are both wrong here, and they are the commonest error Czech writers make in this frame.
cards.body_cz: Vše o tvaru pokrývají tři pravidla a každé z nich vypadá kdekoli jinde v angličtině jako chyba. Za prvé, sloveso má holý základní tvar — žádné -s ve třetí osobě. Za druhé, be je tvarem pro všechny osoby a trpný rod tvoří be a příčestí minulé tam, kde by běžná věta potřebovala is nebo was. Za třetí, zápor tvoří holé not před slovesem zcela bez pomocného slovesa: that he not be told. Does not i doesn't jsou zde chybné a právě to je nejčastější chyba českých pisatelů v této vazbě.

table.caption: what the clause looks like
rows: it was vital that he be there
it was vital that he was there

points: There is no do-support anywhere in this clause, in the negative or elsewhere.
A plural subject takes be as well: that the rules be the same for each team.
The passive and the negative combine in the obvious way: that the price not be increased.

cards.title: Were, and the phrases that kept it
cards.title_cz: Were a fráze, které je uchovaly
cards.body: Were is the one past subjunctive still in use. After if it marks a hypothesis as remote for every person, including I and he: if I were you, if it were not for her help. Were to plus the base form pushes it further away still — if the company were to close is more distant and more careful than if the company closed, which is why it belongs to cautious writing. Everything else the old subjunctive left behind is fixed: be that as it may, come what may, if need be, suffice it to say, far be it from me, as it were. Learn each whole; none of them can be taken apart. Lest is the last survivor with a live rule — it is formal and takes the base form.
cards.body_cz: Were je jediný dosud užívaný minulý konjunktiv. Po if označuje domněnku za vzdálenou pro všechny osoby včetně I a he: if I were you, if it were not for her help. Vazba were to se základním tvarem ji posouvá ještě dál — if the company were to close je vzdálenější a opatrnější než if the company closed, a proto patří do obezřetného psaní. Vše ostatní, co po starém konjunktivu zbylo, je ustálené: be that as it may, come what may, if need be, suffice it to say, far be it from me, as it were. Každý výraz se učte vcelku, žádný nelze rozebrat. Posledním přeživším s živým pravidlem je lest — je formální a pojí se se základním tvarem.

table.caption: the survivors
rows: if it turns out to be necessary
I will not go into detail
apologises for a figure of speech

points: Was for were after if is normal in speech; were is the safer choice in writing.
Were to needs a to-infinitive: if he were to ask, never if he were ask.
The inverted order — were it not for, were I to — is the same grammar fronted; that pattern belongs to the inversion unit.

items.en: It is essential that he arrive on time.
items.cz: Je nezbytné, aby přišel včas.
items.gap: It is ____ that he arrive on time.
accepts: It is essential that he arrive on time.
It's essential that he arrive on time.
items.explanation: A short list of adjectives of necessity — essential, vital, important, imperative, crucial, necessary, advisable, desirable — takes a that-clause whose verb goes into the base form, no matter who the subject is and no matter what tense the trigger is in. It is essential that he arrive on time, not that he arrives. The -s simply does not appear, and be stays be. This is the mandative subjunctive, and English keeps it alive almost entirely in this frame. Two traps follow. A past trigger changes nothing: it was essential that he arrive keeps the base form. And an adjective of fact rather than of necessity takes the ordinary indicative instead — it is clear that he knows the rules. Czech marks the whole distinction with aby, which is why the frame is easy to recognise and hard to produce: there is no Czech verb ending to copy across.
items.explanation_cz: Krátký seznam přídavných jmen nutnosti — essential, vital, important, imperative, crucial, necessary, advisable, desirable — si žádá vedlejší větu s that, jejíž sloveso stojí v základním tvaru, bez ohledu na podmět i na čas věty řídící. It is essential that he arrive on time, nikoli that he arrives. Koncovka -s se prostě neobjeví a be zůstává be. Jde o takzvaný mandativní konjunktiv a angličtina jej udržuje při životě téměř výhradně v této vazbě. Plynou z toho dvě nástrahy. Minulý čas ve větě řídící nemění nic: it was essential that he arrive si základní tvar ponechává. A přídavné jméno faktu, nikoli nutnosti, si žádá běžný oznamovací způsob — it is clear that he knows the rules. Čeština celý rozdíl vyjadřuje spojkou aby, a proto se vazba snadno pozná a těžko tvoří: není zde žádná česká koncovka, kterou by šlo přenést.

items.explanation: Were is the one past subjunctive English still has, and it does two jobs. After if it marks a hypothesis as remote or unreal for every person, including I and he — if I were you, if it were not for her help. Followed by to plus the base it pushes the hypothesis further off still: if the company were to close is a more distant, more careful supposition than if the company closed. Beyond that, the old subjunctive survives only in fixed expressions that are learnt whole and never taken apart — be that as it may, come what may, if need be, suffice it to say, far be it from me — and after lest, which is formal and takes the base form. As it were is the hedge in the set: it apologises for a figure of speech.
items.explanation_cz: Were je jediný minulý konjunktiv, který angličtině zbyl, a plní dvě úlohy. Po if označuje domněnku za vzdálenou nebo nereálnou pro všechny osoby včetně I a he — if I were you, if it were not for her help. Ve spojení s to a základním tvarem posouvá domněnku ještě dál: if the company were to close je vzdálenější a opatrnější úvaha než if the company closed. Jinak starý konjunktiv přežívá jen v ustálených výrazech, které se učí vcelku a nikdy se nerozebírají — be that as it may, come what may, if need be, suffice it to say, far be it from me — a po spojce lest, jež je formální a pojí se se základním tvarem. As it were je v této skupině změkčovadlem: omlouvá se za obrazné vyjádření.

items.explanation: Were is the one past subjunctive English still has, and it does two jobs. After if it marks a hypothesis as remote or unreal for every person, including I and he — if I were you, if it were not for her help. Followed by to plus the base it pushes the hypothesis further off still: if the company were to close is a more distant, more careful supposition than if the company closed. Beyond that, the old subjunctive survives only in fixed expressions that are learnt whole and never taken apart — be that as it may, come what may, if need be, suffice it to say, far be it from me — and after lest, which is formal and takes the base form. As it were is the hedge in the set: it apologises for a figure of speech.
items.explanation_cz: Were je jediný minulý konjunktiv, který angličtině zbyl, a plní dvě úlohy. Po if označuje domněnku za vzdálenou nebo nereálnou pro všechny osoby včetně I a he — if I were you, if it were not for her help. Ve spojení s to a základním tvarem posouvá domněnku ještě dál: if the company were to close je vzdálenější a opatrnější úvaha než if the company closed. Jinak starý konjunktiv přežívá jen v ustálených výrazech, které se učí vcelku a nikdy se nerozebírají — be that as it may, come what may, if need be, suffice it to say, far be it from me — a po spojce lest, jež je formální a pojí se se základním tvarem. As it were je v této skupině změkčovadlem: omlouvá se za obrazné vyjádření.
